--- title: "Multivariate Copulas & Cross-Modal Aggregation" description: "Copula families, auto-selection, joint sampling, and multivariate forecasting" date: today format: html: self-contained: true embed-resources: true code-fold: true code-tools: true --- When forecasting **multiple targets simultaneously**, their joint distribution matters. This tutorial explores: 1. **Copula families** — model different types of inter-target dependence 2. **Auto-selection** — let BIC choose the best copula from data 3. **Joint sampling** — generate correlated samples from copula-aware predictions 4. **Cross-modal aggregation** — combine predictions from different feature groups We use the **synthetic multivariate** dataset with 3 target columns (y1, y2, y3). ::: {#setup .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import polars as pl from uncertainty_flow.multivariate import GaussianCopula from uncertainty_flow.multivariate.copula import ( ClaytonCopula, FrankCopula, GumbelCopula, auto_select_copula, ) from uncertainty_flow.utils.split import select_validation_plan ``` ::: ::: {#cell-load-data .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} df = pl.read_parquet("../data/synthetic_multivariate.parquet") print(f"Shape: {df.shape}") df.head(5) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Shape: (5000, 7) ``` ::: ::: {#load-data .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {#split .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} targets = ["y1", "y2", "y3"] features = [c for c in df.columns if c not in targets] plan = select_validation_plan(df, task_type="tabular", holdout_fraction=0.2, random_state=42) train, test = plan.outer_split print(f"Plan: {plan.metadata.strategy_name} | Features: {features} | Targets: {targets} | Train: {len(train)} | Test: {len(test)}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Plan: random_holdout | Features: ['x0', 'x1', 'x2', 'x3'] | Targets: ['y1', 'y2', 'y3'] | Train: 4000 | Test: 1000 ``` ::: ::: ## 1. Copula Family Comparison ::: {#cell-copula-comparison .cell cache='true' execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} residuals = train.select(targets).to_numpy() families = { "Gaussian (linear)": GaussianCopula(), "Clayton (lower tail)": ClaytonCopula(), "Gumbel (upper tail)": GumbelCopula(), "Frank (symmetric)": FrankCopula(), } fitted = {} for name, copula in families.items(): try: copula.fit(residuals[:, :2]) fitted[name] = copula except Exception: fitted[name] = None results = [] for name, copula in fitted.items(): if copula is not None: ll = copula.log_likelihood(residuals[:, :2]) results.append( {"family": name, "theta": round(copula.theta_, 4), "log_likelihood": round(ll, 2)} ) else: results.append({"family": name, "theta": None, "log_likelihood": None}) pl.DataFrame(results) ``` ::: {#copula-comparison .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}

Joint Sampling from Copulas ::: {#cell-joint-sampling .cell cache='true' execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} import matplotlib.pyplot as plt copula_gauss = GaussianCopula() copula_gauss.fit(residuals[:, :2]) n_q = 11 quantile_levels = np.linspace(0.05, 0.95, n_q) marginals = np.zeros((1, 2, n_q)) for t in range(2): for qi, q in enumerate(quantile_levels): marginals[0, t, qi] = np.quantile(residuals[:, t], q) joint_samples = copula_gauss.sample( marginals, n_samples=1000, quantile_levels=quantile_levels, random_state=42, ) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6)) if joint_samples.ndim == 3: s1 = joint_samples[0, :, 0] s2 = joint_samples[0, :, 1] else: s1 = joint_samples[:, 0] s2 = joint_samples[:, 1] ax.scatter(s1, s2, alpha=0.3, s=5) ax.set_xlabel("Target y1") ax.set_ylabel("Target y2") ax.set_title(f"Gaussian Copula Joint Samples (n={len(s1)})") plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](05_multivariate_copulas_files/figure-html/joint-sampling-output-1.png){#joint-sampling width=758 height=566} ::: ::: ::: {#cell-correlation-matrix .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} copula_full = GaussianCopula() copula_full.fit(residuals) corr = copula_full.correlation_matrix_ fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5)) im = ax.imshow(corr, cmap="coolwarm", vmin=-1, vmax=1) ax.set_xticks(range(3)) ax.set_yticks(range(3)) ax.set_xticklabels(["y1", "y2", "y3"]) ax.set_yticklabels(["y1", "y2", "y3"]) ax.set_title("Inter-Target Correlation Matrix") fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax) plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](05_multivariate_copulas_files/figure-html/correlation-matrix-output-1.png){#correlation-matrix width=558 height=477} ::: ::: ## 3. QuantileForestForecaster with Copula-Aware Joint Forecasts ::: {#train-multivariate .cell cache='true' execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} from uncertainty_flow.models import QuantileForestForecaster mv_model = QuantileForestForecaster( targets=targets, horizon=1, n_estimators=100, copula_family="auto", auto_tune=False, random_state=42, ) mv_model.fit(train) mv_pred = mv_model.predict(test) mv_interval = mv_pred.interval(confidence=0.9) print("Multivariate model fitted successfully") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Multivariate model fitted successfully ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` /Users/minghao/Desktop/personal/uncertainty_flow/uncertainty_flow/models/quantile_forest.py:240: UncertaintyFlowWarning: Auto-selecting copula for 3D data. Only Gaussian copula supports dimensions > 2.
